name: traceroute
description: Print the route packets take to network host

name: --help
-h
options.description: Show help for traceroute

options.name: -a
options.description: Turn on AS# lookups for each hop encountered

options.name: -A
options.description: Turn on AS# lookups and use the given server instead of the default

options.name: -d
options.description: Enable socket level debugging

options.name: -D
options.description: When an ICMP response to our probe datagram is received, print the differences between the transmitted packet and the packet quoted by the ICMP response.

options.name: -e
options.description: Firewall evasion mode. Use fixed destination ports for UDP and TCP probes. The destination port does NOT increment with each packet sent

options.name: -f
options.description: Set the initial time-to-live used in the first outgoing probe packet

options.name: -F
options.description: Set the `don't fragment` bit

options.name: -g
options.description: Specify a loose source route gateway (8 maximum)

options.name: -i
options.description: Specify a network interface to obtain the source IP address for outgoing probe packets. This is normally only useful on a multihomed host.

options.name: -I
options.description: Use ICMP ECHO instead of UDP datagrams. (A synonym for `-P icmp`)

options.name: -M
options.description: Set the initial time-to-live value used in outgoing probe packets. The default is 1, i.e., start with the first hop

options.name: -m
options.description: Set the max time-to-live (max number of hops) used in outgoing probe packets. The default is net.inet.ip.ttl hops (the same default used for TCP connections)

options.name: -n
options.description: Print hop addresses numerically rather than symbolically and numerically (saves a nameserver address-to-name lookup for each gateway found on the path)

options.name: -P
options.description: Send packets of specified IP protocol. The currently supported protocols are: UDP, TCP, GRE and ICMP Other protocols may also be specified (either by name or by…

options.name: -p
options.description: Protocol specific. For UDP and TCP, sets the base port number used in probes (default is 33434).

options.name: -q
options.description: Set the number of probes per ``ttl'' to nqueries (default is three probes)

options.name: -r
options.description: Bypass the normal routing tables and send directly to a host on an attached network. If the host is not on a directly-attached network, an error is returned.

options.name: -s
options.description: Use the following IP address (which must be given as an IP number, not a hostname) as the source address in outgoing probe packets.

options.name: -S
options.description: Print a summary of how many probes were not answered for each hop

options.name: -t
options.description: Set the type-of-service in probe packets to the following value (default zero). The value must be a decimal integer in the range 0 to 255.

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose output. Received ICMP packets other than TIME_EXCEEDED and UNREACHABLEs are listed

options.name: -w
options.description: Set the time (in seconds) to wait for a response to a probe (default 5 sec.)

options.name: -x
options.description: Toggle IP checksums. Normally, this prevents traceroute from calculating IP checksums.

options.name: -z
options.description: Set the time (in milliseconds) to pause between probes (default 0). Some systems such as Solaris and routers such as Ciscos rate limit ICMP messages.
